clue.text: Seal is broken, disclosing passages

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so the letters of seal and is are reassembled

explanation.surface: A wax seal is cracked, revealing secret passages behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges SEAL plus IS; 'disclosing' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aisles are walkways between rows of seats or shelves, a kind of corridor.

clue.text: Cut down a dentist's work

parts.note: a bridge is a dental appliance fitting false teeth to neighbouring ones

explanation.surface: Someone reduces the cost of a dental job.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, so it is cut down in length.

clue.text: Shipmates set out in this vessel

indicators.note: set out here means arranged afresh, so the letters of shipmates are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: Crew members embark on a voyage aboard their ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship is a boat driven by steam power, a type of seagoing craft.

clue.text: Left in play

parts.note: a stage direction in a script recording that several actors departed the stage

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage direction meaning 'they go out' is printed when characters quit the scene.

clue.text: A supporter of the arts

parts.note: reads like a patron, but means a base that literally holds up a statue or vase

explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the plinth on which a sculpture stands, physically bearing works of art.

clue.text: They may be inflated, say, to being very large

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated eg
OS stands for outsize, the clothing label for very large sizes

explanation.surface: Balloons may be blown up to an enormous size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link joining EG and OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-esteem can swell, and inflated self-images are a common phrase for vanity.

clue.text: Work-out cut without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for cut goes around the hesitation

parts.note: excise means cut out or remove surgically
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A gym session trimmed down with no pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here carries its old sense of outside, so the cut wraps round the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise is physical training, the same thing as a session at the gym.

clue.text: Sum for a small child, a learner

parts.note: a tot is a toddler
L is the learner driver's plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: Simple arithmetic set for a toddler who is just learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the amount reached by adding figures together.

clue.text: Still getting in after hours, showing childish habits

indicators.note: getting in tells us one word goes inside the other

parts.note: late means after the usual time
yet as in 'still', up to now

explanation.surface: A child keeps coming home late and behaving immaturely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' means clothing, as in a riding habit; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the full set of clothes and bedding for a newborn baby.

clue.text: Joint may be worn out

definitions.meaning: a short thick double-breasted jacket put on to go outdoors

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a marijuana cigarette and a sailor's heavy jacket worn outside.

clue.text: Guy on board gives warning shout to stop

parts.note: fore is the golfer's cry to warn people of a ball
stay means remain or halt

explanation.surface: A man on a ship shouts a warning to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is a rope steadying a mast, not a man; 'gives' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A forestay is a rope or wire running from the masthead to the bow, a ship's guy line.

clue.text: Settle score

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to write music

explanation.definitionFit: One can calm oneself down, and a composer writes music by the same verb.

clue.text: Act before an underling gains control

indicators.note: before places the word for act ahead of the word for underling

parts.note: do means act or perform
a minion is a servile subordinate

explanation.surface: Someone acts first, before a subordinate seizes power.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion means sovereignty or authority over territory or people.

clue.text: One way to work with figures

definitions.text: One way to work with figures

parts.words: One way to work with figures
parts.note: suggests arithmetic, but the figures are statues and the work is carving

explanation.definitionFit: To sculpt is to carve or model statues, shaping human forms in stone or clay.

clue.text: Weak case made for charitable collection

parts.note: poor means feeble or of low quality
a box is a container or case

explanation.surface: A feeble argument is made in support of collecting for charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made for' is a link joining the two pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A box in a church for alms donations is gathered for the needy.

clue.text: Repeat after some reflection

parts.note: a sound returning once it has bounced off a surface, not a thought-out reply

explanation.definitionFit: A reverberation is sound heard again after bouncing off a wall or cliff.

clue.text: Ideal setting for production of "Pinafore"?

parts.note: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta; a pinafore is a kind of apron, so the jokey venue is the forestage named after it

explanation.definitionFit: The forward part of a theatre stage in front of the curtain shares its name with a pinafore-like garment.

clue.text: Stopping for a breather in boxing arena

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the arena surrounds the breather

parts.note: a ring is a boxing or circus arena
a rest is a short break

explanation.surface: A boxer pauses for breath in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport, but signals containment; 'for' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Arresting means bringing to a halt, as in arresting a decline.

clue.text: Water a mother's beer

parts.note: dam is a mother animal, here with the possessive
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone dilutes their mother's pint with water.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a jocular old term for drinking water, the first man's only drink.

clue.text: Evergreen plant Iris adapts in new arrangement

indicators.note: in new arrangement says the letters of iris and adapts are reordered

explanation.surface: An iris is adapted into a fresh floral display with an evergreen.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy leafy houseplant that stays green all year.

clue.text: Cooked sausage to relieve hunger

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of sausage are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A fried sausage to satisfy one's appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage is to ease or satisfy an appetite or longing, the classic collocation being with hunger.

clue.text: Flag of many colours

definitions.meaning: the yellow flag is a wild waterside plant of that genus
the Greek messenger goddess of the rainbow, whose name gives the word for iridescence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is a plant, not a banner; the second sense is the rainbow goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant genus includes the wild yellow flag, and its name comes from the Greek rainbow goddess.

clue.text: Arresting stranger in the street

indicators.note: in places the stranger inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner or stranger

explanation.surface: Police detain a foreigner on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arresting' sounds like police work but means striking; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means prominent or striking, catching the eye just as something arresting does.

clue.text: John, half-gone on the bottle, is jolly

indicators.note: half-gone says only the front half of the name remains

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: John, half drunk from the bottle, is in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the bottle' suggests drinking, but 'on' just means the bottle follows; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jovial means cheerful and good-humoured, full of merriment.

clue.text: Group in second year displaying risqué behaviour?

indicators.note: in places the group between the two abbreviations

parts.note: a team is a group working together

explanation.surface: A set of second-year students behaving rather saucily.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy means erotic or sexy, as in a racy love scene.

clue.text: Law and order

explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official proclamation from a ruler, both a decree and a command.

clue.text: Enormous leakage in fuel

indicators.note: in puts the leakage inside the fuel

parts.note: coal is a fuel
loss as in a leak or wastage

explanation.surface: A huge leak in the fuel supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means huge, after the giant Colossus of Rhodes.

clue.text: Show displeasure when nothing is in place

indicators.note: in puts the nothing inside the word for place

parts.note: put means place or set down
O is the zero figure for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone sulks because nothing is where it should be.
explanation.definitionFit: To pout is to push out the lips in sulkiness.

clue.text: A good mixer, maybe, but a trouble-maker

definitions.meaning: a device that stirs liquids, like a washing machine paddle

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a stirring machine and a political stirrer.

clue.text: Look pleased about one literary comparison

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the expression goes around the numeral

parts.note: to smile is to look happy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone looks pleased about a single figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile is a figure of speech likening one thing to another with like or as.

clue.text: Appeal for admittance when about to dine

indicators.note: about here means around, so admittance wraps the eating

parts.note: entry is admission
eat means dine

explanation.surface: A plea to be let in when someone is about to have dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to dine' reads as 'soon to eat'; instead 'about' means the admittance goes around the dining. 'for', 'when' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or plea.

clue.text: Come down on fire

definitions.meaning: to dismount or descend from a vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to get off a bus or land, and alight also means burning.
